tagline: A leading financial services firm based in the United States, with operations worldwide.
hero_kpi_rationale: The loan book is the primary driver of net interest income (NII), the historical core of banking profitability. For JPMorgan, its massive scale and credit quality make it a key indicator of balance sheet strength.
company_description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. operates as a bank and financial holding company in the United States, rest of North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, Latin America, and the Caribbean. It operates in three segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management. The company offers deposit, investment and lending products, and cash management; mortgage origination and servicing activities; residential mortgages and home equity loans; and credit cards, payment solutions, travel services, merchant offers, lifestyle benefits, auto loans, and leases to consumers and small businesses through bank branches, ATMs, and digital and telephone banking. It also provides investment banking, market-making, financing, custody, and securities products and services; corporate strategy and structure advisory, equity and debt market capital-raising, and loan origination and syndication services; cash and derivative instruments, risk management solutions, prime brokerage, clearing, and research; and fund services, liquidity and trading services, and data solutions products for large corporations, financial institutions, merchants, start-ups, sm

kpis.name: Loan Book
kpis.explanation: Total amount of loans extended by the bank to its customers.
kpis.description: The loan book grew in 2025, supported by the CIB and CCB segments, despite tighter credit conditions.
kpis.signal: Strong loan book growth despite a high-interest-rate environment.

kpis.name: Net Interest Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between interest income earned and borrowing costs, as a percentage of earning assets.
kpis.description: NIM increased in 2025, driven by higher interest rates on loans and prudent deposit management.
kpis.signal: Margin improvement due to optimized interest rate management.

kpis.name: Return on Equity
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by shareholders' equity, measures profitability for shareholders.
kpis.description: JPMorgan maintains a high ROE, supported by disciplined cost management and strong revenue generation.
kpis.signal: High ROE, above sector target, reflecting strong operational performance.

kpis.name: Common Equity Tier 1 Ratio
kpis.explanation: Measures the bank's financial strength by comparing its core equity capital to risk-weighted assets.
kpis.description: The CET1 ratio remains well above regulatory requirements, reinforcing investor confidence.
kpis.signal: High ratio, enabling share buybacks and generous dividends.

kpis.name: Cost-to-Income Ratio
kpis.explanation: Proportion of costs to total revenues: the lower, the more efficient the bank.
kpis.description: The ratio improved as revenue growth outpaced cost increases, despite investments in digital capabilities.
kpis.signal: Improving operational efficiency despite technological investments.

kpis.name: Assets Under Management (Wealth Management)
kpis.explanation: Total assets managed for wealthy clients through the Asset & Wealth Management division.
kpis.description: AWM continues gaining market share due to differentiated offerings and a strong institutional client base.
kpis.signal: Robust AUM growth, driven by positive net flows and market performance.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $182.447 billion in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of $57.048 billion in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $3.0 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $16.625 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 29.1% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Cumulative Share Buybacks
kpis.explanation: Total share buybacks announced over multiple years, reflecting capital return policy.
kpis.description: JPMorgan has maintained a high pace of buybacks, supported by strong earnings generation and a high CET1 ratio.
kpis.signal: Strong commitment to capital return despite the regulatory environment.

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares outstanding during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate profit per share: basis for Payout Ratio calculation (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Major Legal and Regulatory Risks
risks.summary: JPM is exposed to strict and evolving regulations, with risks of sanctions, operational restrictions, and increased costs.
risks.score_rationale: Central position in the 10-K, mentioned first and detailed across several pages. Strong language: 'materially and adversely affect', 'heightened regulatory scrutiny'. Regulation is tightening for large banks like JPM. Category heavily weighted in the financial sector. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Government Litigation and Investigations
risks.summary: JPM faces numerous legal actions and investigations, potentially leading to heavy fines, restrictions, and reputational damage.
risks.score_rationale: Presented as a recurring and costly risk. Mentions of significant penalties, multiple lawsuits, and admissions of fault. Trend of increasing formal actions. Direct impact on reputation and financial results. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Cyberattacks or Operational Failures
risks.summary: A successful cyberattack or system failure could disrupt operations, compromise data security, and damage JPM's reputation.
risks.score_rationale: Cited among operational risks as capable of causing severe harm. Language: 'harm that could be caused by a successful cyber attack'. Dependence on critical systems. Risk amplified by increasing digitalization. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Credit Risks Related to Economic Conditions
risks.summary: An economic downturn could increase credit defaults and reduce collateral values, weighing on profitability.
risks.score_rationale: Clear mention of risks tied to deterioration in clients' financial condition and collateral value. Linked to unfavorable economic conditions. Less existential than regulatory or legal risks, but significant in adverse cycles. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Liquidity and Credit Rating Risks
risks.summary: Any pressure on liquidity or a downgrade in credit rating could increase funding costs and limit business activities.
risks.score_rationale: Presented as critical: reliance on subsidiaries for funding, risk of rating downgrades. Loss of liquidity could paralyze operations. Language: 'constrained liquidity' and 'adverse effects'. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Operational and Internal Control Risks
risks.summary: Failures in systems, controls, or data management could lead to losses, errors, or sanctions.
risks.score_rationale: Risk covering systems, employees, vendors, and data management. Mentions of flaws in stress testing models and reporting. Language: 'adverse effects' and 'harm'. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Climate Change-Related Risks
risks.summary: Climate change could affect client solvency and constrain financing activities in certain sectors.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in strategic risks as having potential adverse impacts on clients and operations. Language less alarming: 'potential adverse impacts'. Less immediate than others, but growing in relevance. (default score, to be refined)
